text:
lina: Quick sync — customer asked for a higher-throughput embeddings endpoint for search/rerank. They want predictable latency and bulk upload support. We need to finalize batching limits, supported dims/models, response schema, and launch criteria for a beta in ~4 weeks.

kevin: Can we define a hard latency SLO? e.g. p95 < 200ms for small batches, < 500ms for big batches. This affects max_batch. :thinking_face:

maya: For quality, we should support two default dims: 1536 (fast) and 3072 (higher-quality). Recommend default model mapping: 1536 -> redwood-emb-lite-v1, 3072 -> redwood-emb-pro-v1. Open-models also allowed as opt-in.

alex: Customer asked specifically for up to 10k vectors per upload in a single call (bulk import). Is that realistic for beta? They also want per-item ids in the response.

jordan: Memory / GPU constraints: embeddings are computed token-less but the biggest cost is IO + batching. On our Dedicated clusters, 10k at 1536 is ~60M floats ~240MB per request (float32). With quantized outputs we can reduce, but runtime memory still spikes with batch. Need to cap max_batch per request per model.

lina: Proposal: API-level limits = default_batch=64, max_batch=1024 (with streaming chunking for >1024), max_total_items_per_request=10000 but server will internally chunk and return partial status if throttled. Launch criteria: feature parity for single-item and batch endpoints, docs, SDK examples, smoke tests, and one enterprise customer pilot.

kevin: Implementation note: prefer server-side chunking: accept large array, stream compute in windowed batches (configurable). That hides complexity from client but we must document that order & IDs are preserved.

maya: Also need deterministic normalization steps documented (lowercasing, Unicode NFKC, punctuation handling) — embeddings regressions often due to preprocessing drift. Add a fixed "preprocess_version" field in responses.

alex: Customer also asked about embedding vector format: float32 vs int8 compressed. They want minimal wire size. Can we return base64-encoded compressed bytes as option?

jordan: We can support two response formats: 1) JSON array of floats (human-readable) and 2) compressed base64 (protobuf or raw bytes + simple header). Option controlled by `accept` query or `response_format` param. But compressed path requires compatibility guarantees.

lina: UX decisions to confirm:
- Default dims: 1536
- Extra dim preset: 3072 (opt-in)
- Default batch: 64, server chunk at 1024 window, internal streaming for >1024
- Response formats: `json` (floats) and `base64-zstd` (compressed)
- Models: redwood-emb-lite-v1 (default), redwood-emb-pro-v1, allow open models behind opt-in flag

kevin: For rate limits and quotas: bill by input tokens OR output vector units? Simpler: bill by input tokens + vector-dim factor. Need pricing input from finance.

maya: Eval criteria before launch:
- end-to-end quality parity tests on our eval set (cosine sim + MRR) for both dims
- throughput targets: single-item p95 < 150ms for 1536 on hosted, batch throughput per GPU >= X vectors/sec (we'll run perf runs)
- no memory OOMs during 10k uploads (stress test)

alex: From customer side: they care about stable IDs mapping and partial success reporting (if some items fail). Also monotonic order preservation. Add example of error handling.

lina: Draft error model: top-level `items` array with per-item `status` and `embedding` or `error`. `overall_status` with `partial`/`complete` flags. Include `processing_chunks` hint if chunked.

kevin: Example request/response (dev sketch):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-emb-lite-v1",
  "inputs": [
    {"id": "doc1", "text": "..."},
    {"id": "doc2", "text": "..."},
    ...
  ],
  "response_format": "base64-zstd"  // optional
}

200 OK
{
  "overall_status": "partial",
  "processing_chunks": ["0-1023","1024-2047"],
  "items": [
    {"id":"doc1","status":"ok","embedding":"Aj2...base64..."},
    {"id":"doc2","status":"error","error":"rate_limited"},
    ...
  ],
  "preprocess_version": "2026-03-1"
}
```

maya: We'll need to version the embeddings API (v1) and make clear compatibility guarantees for vector ordering across SDKs.

jordan: Ops concerns: streaming large responses means longer-lived connections. Ensure load balancer idle timeout increased for beta routes, and add metrics: chunk_latency, items_per_request, memory_peak_per_request.

lina: Action items:
- kevin: spike implement server-side chunking & preserve IDs (2d)
- maya: finalize model mapping & prep eval harness (3d)
- jordan: perf + stress tests infra (5d)
- alex: confirm pilot customer SLA + pricing ask (EOD)
- lina: draft beta launch checklist + docs PR (3d)

kevin: ok. I'll prototype the chunking shim today. :thumbsup:

maya: On it. will post perf numbers to this thread when ready. :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for `embeddings/v1` tomorrow 03:00 UTC. (automated note)

lina: Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene after the spikes. :wave:
